data: Tamara has the alchemist gene. She could transform reality if desired, and there are various factions who wish to wield her power. The Queen wants to keep Tamara safe, but in trying to do so, she puts her even more in danger. Bastian knows one of the Queen's friends and Tamara's platonic love, works for one of the factions, so he assumes the Queen only wants to use Tamara.
Bastian is Tamara's friend. He's trying to protect her from the queen, who is her sister. But the queen is also trying to protect Tamara.

This story is set in a future where humanity returns to a sort of medieval system. The machines abandoned earth along with a few chosen humans, believing humanity as a whole was a lost cause. Tamara's gene would allow to use a remaining device and start advancing humanity again, even with its decimated population.

One faction desires to change earth and bring the machines back. They believe rationality and logic are all that is needed. Activating the device would also allow to change the neural connections from every human on earth.
One faction wants to make sure the device is never used, so they want to kill Tamara. They believe humans have to pay for their sins.

One faction wants to use the device to call up the first humans back to earth. A race which left long before the rise of the machines or even civilized society. A race who could guide humanity to a future that blends emotion and logic. A race who understands the dance between yin and yang.

Bastian doesn't belong to any of those factions, all he cares about is protecting Tamara. He doesn't trust anyone since his father died protecting the device. Bastian and Tamara are connected. He comes from a line of guardians, protection the device and the gene lineage. He doesn't know the lineage derives from the first humans, a way for them to know when humanity would be ready for their return.

Lea, the queen's friend, belongs to the rational faction. She comes from a lineage of warriors who believe the only salvation is the machines ruling. They believe the machines left as a rational outcome of having to endure emotional beings. Lea wants to activate the device hoping the neural changes will erase the pain she feels. But Lea doesn't know her lineage precedes the machines, it descends from the first people, a faction who chose to stay on earth and fight for their race believing humanity has a chance.

Tamara is a soul lost between worlds. She wants to heal humanity but doesn't know how. She's afraid she could lose herself, since her responsibility is so big she has to keep her darkness under control.
The device transforms Tamara biologically and psychologically. The transformation depends on the side of Tamara which overpowers the other: dark or light.
